blocks.content: Course: API Handling with Asynchronous Javascript
So you've experienced first-hand what blocking looks like and why it hurts the user experience. You faced such problems because JavaScript:

items: Runs code from top to bottom
Executes one line at a time
Finishes one task before it starts the next

blocks.content: Moreover, JavaScript is built on the following pillars:

items: It doesn't run code in parallel.
It finishes one task before starting the next.

blocks.content: This way of executing code is called single threaded execution, and the typical behavior exhibited by JavaScript is called synchronous behavior.
